_meta.description: Research encoding of referral criteria for breast, ovarian, endometrial (post-menopausal bleeding) and cervical symptoms. Paraphrased from NICE NG12 (Suspected cancer: recognition and referral) and NICE CKS guidance. This is an approximation for a research prototype and has NOT been clinically reviewed. Do not use for patient care.
_meta.persistence_rule: A symptom is treated as persistent if reported for >= 21 days or described with frequency words (daily, always, most days). NG12 ovarian guidance uses 'persistently or frequently, particularly more than 12 times per month'; 21 days is our operational proxy.

criteria.action: Suspected cancer pathway referral (appointment within 2 weeks).
Non-urgent clinical review of an unexplained breast lump.
Suspected cancer pathway referral for nipple changes in one nipple only, age 50+.
Consider suspected cancer pathway referral for skin changes suggestive of breast cancer.
Consider suspected cancer pathway referral for an unexplained lump in the armpit, age 30+.
Urgent referral if a pelvic/abdominal mass or fluid in the abdomen is found.
Primary-care tests (CA125 blood test, then pelvic ultrasound if raised).
Consider CA125 testing for new IBS-like symptoms at age 50+.
Suspected cancer pathway referral for post-menopausal bleeding, age 55+.
Consider suspected cancer pathway referral for post-menopausal bleeding under 55.
Clinical examination of the cervix (speculum examination) soon.
Clinical examination for persistent bleeding between periods.
Clinical examination for persistent unusual (e.g. blood-stained or foul-smelling) discharge.

age_band.question: Which age group are you in?

persistent.question: Have the symptoms been present for 3 weeks or more, or on most days?

unilateral.question: Is the nipple change unilateral (one side only)?

safety_net.breast: Seek clinical review for any new breast lump, skin dimpling, nipple retraction, or unilateral nipple discharge.
safety_net.cervical: Seek clinical review for post-coital bleeding, intermenstrual bleeding, or persistent abnormal vaginal discharge.
safety_net.ovarian: Seek clinical review if abdominal distension, early satiety, pelvic pain or urinary urgency persist for 3 weeks or more.
safety_net.endometrial: Any post-menopausal bleeding (more than 12 months after the last period) requires clinical assessment.
